answer: At a season's start, each identity seals with its quill a private plan for every possible public signal: if the cedar market spikes, do X; if it crashes, do Y; if it stalls, do Z. Weeks later one signal actually fires, chosen unpredictably, and each identity must execute its matching branch within hours, showing the sealed plan. One honest agent writes only its own few branches. A farm must author genuinely different plans for every alias times every branch, or reuse plans and collide identically when opened — so scale multiplies real foresight work instead of copying it.
